messages:
zoe_ops: quick heads-up — since ~06:00 UTC we've seen sustained read IOPS on /dev/nvme0n1 in eu-west-1 nodes causing gpu-attach latency to spike (pods stuck in Pending for ~30-90s).

mike_infra: saw it too, gpu provisioning queue length up by ~18% across the fleet. correlates with higher scrub activity on scratchpool. link to dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/boards/evict-iops?panel=nvme0n1

elaine_storage: i pulled iostat on one affected host, here's the snippet:
```
Device:         r/s   w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1     3200.4 12.3  245000  9800    77.6     6.8     2.1    0.3   98.7
```

elaine_storage: %util ~99, avg queue length high — looks like scrub/cleaner saturating the device. not seeing firmware errors, SMART fine.

zoe_ops: @raj_sre can you confirm if eviction/janitor runs are overlapping with batch window? we had a scheduler tweak last-week that moved some windows earlier.

raj_sre: yep, night-scrub cron for eu-west got bumped to 05:45 during the rollout. that collides with morning batch provisioning. not ideal.

mike_infra: options: 1) throttle janitor concurrency on eu-west (cheap quick fix), 2) push scrub window later, 3) add I/O cgroups to janitor to cap iops/bandwidth, 4) patch scheduler to avoid gpu-attach windows.

elaine_storage: i prefer 3 for long-term, but it needs careful tuning. can do 1+2 immediately. throttling from default 4 -> 1 reduced peak on a canary earlier (reduced cost but slowed cleanup).

janitor-bot: janitor scheduled run starting 2026-03-21T05:45:02Z on pool eu-west-1-scratch (concurrency=4) :wrench:

zoe_ops: ok let's do quick mitigation: throttle concurrency to 1 for eu-west for next 6h and move cron to 02:00 UTC. mike, can you push a canary?

mike_infra: yes. pushing canary change to janitor-deploy(eu-west) now — will route 10% of jobs through new config. logs: `kubectl apply -f janitor-config-eu-west.yaml`

elaine_storage: after throttle there's an expected backlog growth. estimate: +~12% ephemeral usage after 24h if we keep concurrency=1. cost tradeoff: small increase in reserve usage vs avoiding gpu attach failures (which cost more).

raj_sre: i'll add a temporary alert to mute the gpu-attach flapping pager and create a follow-up to revert if attach latency goes back to normal. alert id: infra-evict-iops-eu-west-2026-03

mike_infra: canary applied — 10% traffic shows device util dropped to ~65% and attach latency improved on those hosts. rolling to 50% now.

zoe_ops: nice. plan: keep concurrency=1 for 6h, move cron to 02:00, follow up with a task to implement io cgroups on janitor (EL: elaine), and run a perf test to find safe iops cap. postmortem task created: #TICK-2483.

elaine_storage: noted, i'll own the io-cgroup task and schedule a perf run tomorrow (small canary cluster). also will draft a config for dynamic throttle based on %util.

raj_sre: leaving the temporary alert in place for 12h and will annotate the incident channel. once metrics are stable we'll rollback the pager.

zoe_ops: thanks team :thumbsup: — keeping this thread as the single source. i'll update status in #release-war-room if anything changes.

mike_infra: one more small datapoint — i found two nodes with high scrub overlap because their timezone labels were wrong, fixed the labels and rescheduled. might explain why the hit was concentrated to a subset.

elaine_storage: good catch. i'll add a check to the janitor workflow to assert node-zone/cron alignment.

zoe_ops: closing interim mitigation. last check at 06:28 UTC looks stable. reopen if we see >80% util again.
